10.1002_adfm.75527: Efficient photocatalytic overall water splitting is often constrained by the fundamental trade‐off between charge separation efficiency and redox driving force in conventional heterojunctions. Direct Z‐scheme architectures theoretically resolve this dilemma, yet constructing robust, defect‐free interfaces remains a formidable synthetic challenge. Here, we introduce a sonochemical strategy in which transient cavitation drives the in situ insertion of Zn during the growth of In 2 S 3 on PbTiO 3 , giving rise to interfacial Pb─O─Zn bridges. These Zn bridges convert the junction from type‐II to a direct Z‐scheme, enabling selective interfacial recombination while preserving high oxidation and reduction potentials. Multimodal spectroscopic and density functional theory confirmed the Z‐scheme pathway and prolonged carrier lifetimes. The resulting photocatalyst delivers stoichiometric H 2 and O 2 evolution rates of 166.6 and 81.7 µmol h − 1 , demonstrating a competitive performance within reported Z‐scheme heterostructure‐based photocatalysts. This transient cavitation‐driven heteroatom insertion strategy provides a potentially general and programmable protocol for engineering precise semiconductor interfaces and constructing direct Z‐scheme junctions for solar fuel production.
10.1002_aenm.202506260: All‐solid‐state sodium batteries utilizing sulfide electrolytes and sodium (Na) anodes are promising for energy storage due to their safety and cost‐effectiveness. However, their practical implementation is significantly hindered by the interfacial degradation at Na 3 PS 4 |Na interface, while the resolution strategies remain scarce due to the unclear underlying mechanisms. Herein, operando synchrotron X‐ray computed tomography is utilized to reveal an electro‐chemo‐mechanical coupling failure mechanism. Our results demonstrate the formation of a 65‐µm‐thick side‐reaction layer at the interface within two hours of contact. This electron‐conducting but ion‐blocking layer causes non‐uniform Na electrodeposition, triggering continuous mechanical cracking inward Na 3 PS 4 that leads to a short‐circuit. To address this issue, a thermodynamically stable thin Na 3 Sb‐NaF functional layer is engineered on Na to protect Na 3 PS 4 from being chemically reduced. Its high Na‐ion diffusivity ensures uniform ion transport for homogeneous Na electrodeposition, enabling a mechanically integrated interface. As a result, symmetric cells sustain over 1000 h of cycling at 0.1 mA cm– 2 (0.1 mAh cm −2 ), while full cells using NaNi 1/3 Fe 1/3 Mn 1/3 O 2 cathodes achieve 88.3% capacity retention after 300 cycles at 0.2 C, room temperature. Crucially, anode‐free all‐solid‐state batteries exhibit stable cycling for over 60 cycles. This work advances the development of high‐energy, durable all‐solid‐state sodium metal batteries.
10.1002_aenm.71485: Aqueous Zn‐Te batteries offer high capacity via a six‐electron TeO 2 /Te/ZnTe reaction, yet suffer from low discharge voltage (∼0.6 V) due to the sluggish conversion kinetics and high overpotential of TeO 2 /Te. Although Cl − enables a lower‐overpotential TeCl 4 /Te conversion, the TeCl 4 hydrolysis leads to an unstable high‐voltage discharge plateau at ∼1.2 V. Besides, the accumulation of poorly conductive tellurium halide along charge hinders electron transport between the reaction zone and current collector, leading to inefficient electrochemical oxidation of Te. Here, based on the hard‐soft acid‐base (HSAB) principle, a borderline base Br − is introduced to reconstruct the coordination of the soft acid Te 4+ to form more stable phases and prevent voltage degradation. Meanwhile, Br 3 − is in situ generated via deep charging, which unlocks a chemical oxidation bypass for Te with facile electron transfer at the solid/electrolyte interface. This improves the oxidation efficiency of Te and increases the proportion of high‐voltage plateau capacity during subsequent discharge. A low‐content polyvinyl pyrrolidone addition further improves the capacity retention through its adsorption effect. Accordingly, the Zn‐Te battery delivers high capacities of 837 mAh g −1 at 0.5 A g −1 and 483 mAh g −1 at 5 A g −1 , with more than half capacity stably contributed by the high‐voltage plateau.
10.1002_anie.202517145: The slow kinetics of the sulfur reduction reaction (SRR) and Li 2 S oxidation reaction (SOR) in lithium‐sulfur batteries (LSBs) seriously affect their practical applications. Herein, we prepared a functional interlayer for LSBs consisting of hydroxylated carbon nanotubes dispersed with NiCoMoIr medium‐entropy alloys embedded in CeO 2 surface materials. Experimental results revealed a bidirectional catalytic mechanism involving different elements, verifying that Ir and Ni promote the SRR of Li 2 S 6 to Li 2 S. Meanwhile, Co and Mo were found to primarily promote the conversion process of Li 2 S to Li 2 S 6 . CeO 2 exhibits a bidirectional synergistic effect on enhancing the kinetics of the SRR and SOR. The battery exhibits a specific capacity of 1535.7 mAh g −1 at 0.2 C, and the decay rate is only 0.051% for per‐cycle of 1000 cycles at 1 C. More importantly, a 2 Ah‐level pouch cell with an energy density of 436.4 Wh kg −1 and the capacity decay rate was 0.039% per‐cycle after 800 cycles.
10.1021_acscatal.5c08247: Electrocatalysis represents a core technology for the conversion and storage of renewable energy. Traditional research has relied heavily on the trial-and-error approach or simple modification of known materials, lacking a guiding framework that can systematically link reaction mechanisms with material design. To address this gap, this review aims to establish a unified, function-oriented integrated design framework. This framework adheres to the core logic of “mechanism-driven demand─function definition─site engineering”: starting from the intrinsic mechanism of the target reaction, it identifies the rate-determining steps and key intermediates; then reversely defines the electronic structure, geometric configuration, and dynamic response characteristics required of active sites; and ultimately guides the rational construction of catalytic materials. Organizing the discourse around the core functions of active sites, this paper systematically analyzes a series of important systems, ranging from hydrogen/oxygen reactions and carbon–nitrogen cycles to the electrocatalytic transformation of organic molecules. By clarifying the inherent correlations between structure, function, and performance across different systems, the review summarizes universal design principles for overcoming the performance limits of conventional materials through the synergistic optimization of multidimensional descriptors and the regulation of dynamic active states. Finally, this paper highlights several emerging research directions, including the rational programming of dynamic active sites, machine learning-assisted inverse design, and the systematic regulation of interfacial microenvironments. It is anticipated that this work will provide a structured methodological guide for advancing electrocatalytic materials from relatively fragmented empirical exploration toward more systematic, rational construction.
